chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When a man supplicates and says after his supplication, 'Whatever Allah willed, there is no might and no strength except with Allah,' Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'My servant has strived and submitted to My command. Fulfill his need.'

key_terms.لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّه: There is no might and no strength except with Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual meaning of saying 'There is no might and no strength except with Allah' after supplication?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the theological balance between human effort (istabsal) and divine decree (istislam) by appending 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah' to supplications. This phrase signifies that while the believer strives, the ultimate power and ability reside solely with Allah, thereby ensuring the acceptance of the dua. It reflects the Imami understanding of tawhid in action, where reliance on God's power complements human agency.
